note: Generated by design/tools/bosses_7_10.py. World units. The page design/bosses/cadence.md is made from this data.
name: Cadence
key: D flat major: D flat, A flat, B flat minor, G flat (I, V, vi, IV)

common.arrives: on the last Drop of its Track and stays until it is dead; the music holds its Drop for the whole fight
common.health: the number given is a first guess: tune it with the careful bot until the fight lasts what the page says with the build a player has by then, as was done for Longwave and The Choir; x (1 + 0.5 per extra player)
common.grid: everything it does lands on the song's grid and is computed from the song's clock, so every device in a co-op run sees the same fight with nothing new on the wire
common.reward: a bonus Trio and Shards for each player; the Track ends
common.crowd: half of the Drop's crowd, fodder only, unless the page says otherwise

parts.name: Pillar (x 4)
parts.what: A ring of twelve petals, radius 90, with its numeral inside in the stroke font (cap 60 wu): I, V, vi, IV. Each has its own hue from the palette: I the peach-gold, V the lavender, vi the periwinkle, IV the mint. Sounding: its petals spread to radius 120, its numeral is white at 2.6 and a pool of its hue lies under it. Silent: petals closed, numeral at 0.8

parts.name: The square
parts.what: The four stand on the corners of a square 700 wu on a side, in the song's order clockwise from the top left (I, V, vi, IV); a thin line in the grid's colour joins them, and the side leading to the next chord brightens over the bar

numbers.follow: the square's centre follows the players' centre at 40 wu/s

phases.name: Progression
rules: The pillar of the bar's chord is open and silent; it is the only one that can be hurt. On the One of its bar it takes x 2 for the beat
The other three each fire a fan of five at the nearest player on beats 1 and 3 (the half-time kick and snare), 180 wu/s
So the open pillar goes round the square one corner a bar, clockwise

phases.name: Modulation
rules: On every fourth bar line, as the song comes back to I, the square turns a quarter turn the other way in one beat, so the next I is where IV stood: the numerals, not the corners, say who is next
Each firing pillar adds a second fan of seven on the snare

phases.name: Inversion
rules: The rule turns over, announced by the word INVERSION and a bar of the bed high-passed: now the sounding pillar is closed and it alone fires, a rosette of sixteen on the One and twelve on three; the other three are open and silent
Three targets at once: the fight ends quickly from here, as a last chorus should

weakPoint: the open pillar, and x 2 on the One of its bar
death: the progression resolves: the four burst in the song's order on the four beats of the last bar and the band holds the tonic chord over a gong
sound: Each pillar is its chord: while it sounds, a pad voice holds its root and the band's stab plays that chord on the One at 1.2
Each firing pillar's fan is a tom on its own chord's root, on one and three: three toms, a slow melody of the chords that are not playing
The turn of the square is a reversed cymbal into the bar line; Inversion is the music bus high-passed at 800 Hz for one bar
Death: the four chords in turn, then the tonic with the gong
